title: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois
note: Malgoire's edition covers §1–37 of roughly 1,600 manuscript pages. The Grothendieck Circle separately holds typed versions of Part Ib and §49. Coverage of the later sections is uneven — this is the clearest case of a work that is famous, partly edited, and still largely untranscribed.

title: Motifs
note: A complete typeset transcription in nineteen sections, dated 30 July 2002 in the document itself. It is not offered here beside the facsimile, because no copy of it is published anywhere this site cites: the Grothendieck Circle lists a typed Motifs — a preliminary text of 1965–1970, taken down by later readers — but supplies it only on request by email. It was formerly attached to folder 12 on the strength of the folder's subject and of editorial judgement; that attachment is withdrawn. Setting nine batches of the Théorie des motifs aside as already edited, on a correspondence nobody has checked and against an edition no reader can open, flattered the count and hid the folder from every queue. Folder 12 is work outstanding again, and will be transcribed. The edition is recorded here because it very probably exists and may well cover those pages — but that is a thing to establish, not to assume.

title: His published writings — EGA, SGA 1–3, FGA, the articles
editors: Alexander Grothendieck, with Jean Dieudonné for EGA (scans: Numdam, Grothendieck Circle)
venue: Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS on Numdam (EGA I–IV, and « On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties »); the Grothendieck Circle's page of published texts for the rest
note: His own published texts, not editions of the fonds — listed because a folder can hold a draft of one. Compared on 26 September 2026 with every folder then transcribed, by reading the texts against the transcriptions rather than by a specialist: no folder is a draft of any of them as a whole. The overlaps are local. Folder 22's typescript (his pp. 26–32) is an earlier version of EGA 0_IV §§19.7–19.8; folder 56's typed leaves are the typescript of SGA 3 Exp. XII, his corrections adopted almost word for word; one page of folder 27 drafts SGA 3 XIII Lemme 4.5; Deligne's letters in folder 23 are the source of errata 8, 9, 12 and 14 to EGA IV. Folders 98, 49, 126 and 128 share statements with the FGA talks (TDTE IV, VI and I), 12 and 15 with « Le groupe de Brauer III » §§9–10, 5 with « Crystals and the De Rham cohomology of schemes », 2 with « La théorie des classes de Chern » §4. And some folders prove what print only announces or leaves open: the semicontinuity inequalities stated without proof in SGA 3 X 8.7 (folder 27), the quasi-finite case of descent TDTE I leaves unanswered (folder 126), the multigaloisian categories SGA 1 V 9 leaves to the reader (folder 29). Leads, not verdicts. The EGA volumes are read from Numdam, which holds the Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS: EGA I (vol. 4), II (8), III (11, 17) and IV (20, 24, 28, 32), and « On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties » (29). The volumes a folder answers are offered beside it as its printed text — IV-1 beside folder 22, IV-4 beside 23, I and II beside 37 — which does not set those folders aside: they are his drafts and working copies, not an edition of them. Beside the EGA volumes, the folders whose overlaps are listed above are shown the printed text they answer: from Numdam where it holds it (the FGA talks in the Séminaire Bourbaki, « La théorie des classes de Chern » and « La théorie de Fredholm » in the Bulletin de la SMF), from the Grothendieck Circle's scans otherwise (SGA 1, the Dix exposés, the Bombay and Nice lectures, the Topology note). The Circle's copies of what Numdam holds are older Numdam files, and are not used.
